headline: Sabalenka survives Noskova 7-6, 3-6, 7-6 and keeps the three-peat alive
whyCareReason: The two-time defending champion dropped a set for the first time here, trailed in the third, and still reached a sixth straight US Open semi-final.
teaser: Aryna Sabalenka def. Linda Noskova 7-6 (7-1), 3-6, 7-6 (10-7) on Ashe. She thought the title defence was over. Then she hit a second-serve ace.
story:
Why this one matters: a three-peat at Flushing Meadows does not survive a quiet afternoon. Sabalenka, chasing a third straight US Open, met Linda Noskova, the new Wimbledon champion, in the quarter-finals and had to go the distance for the first time this fortnight.

BBC logged the score as 7-6 (7-1), 3-6, 7-6 (10-7), a little under two and a half hours. Sabalenka led 5-2 in the first, got broken serving for the set, then ran the breaker 7-1. Noskova took the second 6-3 after a Sabalenka double fault at 30-40. In the third, Noskova held to love for 4-2. Sabalenka won the next three games, then trailed 2-0 in the deciding tie-break before closing it with a second-serve ace. It was her tenth successive tie-break win at this tournament, a run dating to 2021.

She called herself speechless. Nineteen consecutive wins here. First woman since Serena Williams in 2016 to reach six successive US Open semi-finals. Next is Jessica Pegula or Emma Navarro. Noskova hit more winners, made fewer unforced errors, and saved seven of nine break points. Her eleven-match Grand Slam singles streak ends in New York.
stakes: A three-peat stays alive. Wimbledon's new champion goes home. The women's champion is still unwritten.
rivalryAngle: The favourite who thought she was done versus the grass-court shock who had the match at 4-2 in the third.
